While most students who passed drink very little during the week, your level stands out as unusually high and appears to be harming your focus and consistency.

Next, having zero past class failures worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward passing. This is exactly in line with students who succeeded, so the model recognized your solid history as a positive sign.

Your reason for choosing the school—its reputation—also nudged the outcome slightly toward passing. This motivation is fairly common among students who ultimately pass, though it was not strong enough to outweigh the concerns around alcohol use.

To improve, consider cutting back sharply on weekday drinking, as this seems to be the main factor working against you. Protecting your study time and energy could quickly shift your trajectory. With your strong history and clear goals, small changes now can help you pass comfortably and avoid the need for remedial classes next time. (218 words)
